items.title: Captain Price Actor Barry Sloane Says He's the Most Qualified Person to Star in the Call of Duty Movie
items.excerpt: Captain Price actor Barry Sloane wants to be in the Call of Duty movie and believes he's the most qualified person for the job.
items.content_text: Captain Price actor Barry Sloane wants to be in the Call of Duty movie and believes he's the most qualified person for the job. When speaking with Dan Allen Gaming , Sloane was asked if he's interested in reprising his role as Price in the upcoming live-action Call of Duty film. The movie, directed by Peter Berg and written by Taylor Sheridan, is expected to be set in the Modern Warfare universe , but it's unclear if it's a new story or a direct adaptation of one of the games. With that said, it's hard to imagine a Modern Warfare movie without Price. Sloane wants in on the film and even went as far as to say he's the most qualified person on the planet to do it. "I don't think there's anyone else on the planet who is as qualified for the job as I am," said Sloane. "Who has lived the character for almost a decade? Who understands the size of the projects, the love of that fan base, and has been on the journey with them from the get-go? Hollywood is a beast. Sometimes things are decided for certain reasons that can never be understood. But if you're asking me, would I like to do it? Absolutely, I would love to play him in a movie. 100%. That would be fantastic. But let's let the Hollywood cards fall where they land." Sloane also noted that there's been a vocal outpouring from fans to have him play Price in the film, which he massively appreciates. He noted that typically, there's a group of names that a studio wants for a role like this, and they have to go through that process themselves. Nevertheless, he believes he'd be an "asset" to the production if he were to have the opportunity. As games have gotten increasingly realistic, they've also started to use the likenesses of the actors who play them. This has led to demand from fans that film adaptations should use the actors from the games. Of course, Hollywood might make the argument that they're not as big of a box office draw compared to a more traditional mainstream movie star. Whether Call of Duty will utilize the game's cast remains to be seen. Spoilers for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 follow below . Of course, if the Call of Duty movie is canonical to the games, where it falls in the timeline will dictate what characters can show up. Modern Warfare 4 brutally takes a number of characters off the board, including Captain Price. At the end of the game, the character is left to bleed out in the middle of the wilderness, with Ghost having said his goodbyes to his fallen leader. It's a tragic ending for the character, but one that felt right and leaves the future of the Modern Warfare games in question . With that said, if the Call of Duty movie takes place within the canon, it would have to be set before Modern Warfare 4. If it's a sequel of sorts, it may focus on all-new characters or the surviving ones like Ghost and the Korean characters introduced in MW4. The film is due out in 2028, so we'll likely hear more on casting sometime next year as filming nears.

items.title: World of Warcraft Forever Launch Live Blog: It's Looking Like a Smooth Blizzard Launch
items.excerpt: World of Warcraft Forever launch day live blog.
items.content_text: World of Warcraft Forever is finally here, and the gates to this alternate version of Azeroth open at 3 PM PST / 6 PM EST. All the signs from the beta are pointing to Forever being one of the biggest launches in Warcraft history, with so many people testing the game that developers claimed it put up "the craziest numbers" they've seen in 17 years. Even after expanding the level cap in the beta, it was still capped at level 30, and most people – outside of some promotions – had to buy an expensive Skyborne pack to get in. Once the live servers go up, the only barrier to playing WoW Forever is going to be an active WoW subscription or a friend code. (And there are going to be a lot of friend codes out there.) But while WoW Forever promises to be a huge launch and a return to form for many WoW fans, the real test is going to be how well the servers hold up. I've been playing Blizzard's games my entire life, and it's pretty much a given that something is going to go wrong when Blizzard flicks the switch to open up the game. Even last week, when Blizzard opened its name reservation system, European players couldn't get in for hours, and American players were greeted with long server queues and disconnects. So, I expect the full launch to be, well, spicy. But I'm going to be in the trenches, trying to get in myself and keeping an eye on the community to find all the cool stuff people are talking about, and gathering all of that here. So, whether you're stuck at work while the servers go up, or you're inevitably frustrated by the servers buckling under the weight of millions of MMO fans, stay tuned for all the fun. Live updates are below. World of Warcraft Forever Live Blog All times are in EST 7:43 pm: I'm finally on the way to Brill, and as soon as I got past the gate, I rounded a corner, and got blown away by some incredible lighting. Blizzard really did knock the graphics upgrades out of the park with WoW Forever. If you have powerful enough hardware, trust me, max the game out, at least for a little bit. 7:37 pm: Some more problems are starting to appear. In the forums, there's a thread suggesting that there are AMD driver problems that are causing driver timeouts. Let me know down below if you've been running into driver issues. Apparently the problem is a black screen, followed by a hard system reboot. And it looks like this bug has persisted through the beta, according to the player who posted the thread. But this might be a problem on AMD's end, rather than Blizzard. The game is running without issue for me on an Nvidia card. 7:22 pm: There are still people stuck at the ruleset menu, and Blizzard hasn't provided an update on that bug yet. But at least people seem to have a sense of humor about it. How people at the ruleset menu look at people in the login queue. by u/dillcoq in wowforever 7:08 pm: Blizzard is aware of problems with payment processing, so if you're struggling with actually subscribing to the game to play, they're working on it. @RAM2191 As soon as possible! Website issues are due to the amount of traffic, keep trying as you can, maybe even wait just a few minutes. ^CC — Blizzard CS - The Americas (@BlizzardCS) November 4, 2026 7:00 pm: We're an hour into the launch and the servers feel great. No real lag, and I haven't been disconnected yet. I've also seen some reports of new Horde characters being disabled due to the high demand on PvP servers . So much for people not wanting to play monsters . Just speaking anecdotally, but there were so many Undead players that I had to group up with four other people to finish one of the first quests. But, that's exactly what Forever's devs want you to do. 6:36 pm: Just killed enough zombies to finish the first quest, there are just so many people in Tirisfal right now. But, while the launch seems to have gone smoothly for most people, I've started seeing some players that are having trouble getting online. Some people are also reporting that the characters they reserved aren't there anymore . 6:30 pm: IGN's review in progress from Len Hafer just went live! There's obviously no verdict yet, but it seems good so far. 6:23 pm: If you're still getting gray rulesets bug, it seems like most people have been able to fix it by closing the game and re-entering the queue. I know it sucks to have to sit in line again, but it seems like the queues are going pretty quick so far. But, of course, that could change. 6:13 pm: Wait, I'm in! Looks like the server is at least working for me, and there's a veritable army of Undead here in Tirisfal Glades. Even in the forums, people seem pleasantly surprised by how quick the server queue went. But there are still some people who are getting kicked offline as soon as they get to the character select screen. 6:10 pm: Blizzard is aware of the problem with 'Rulesets' not being available, and BlizzardCS has reported it to the devs . Hopefully it's a quick fix. But even though it seems like people are going to have to wait a while to get in, it is kind of nostalgic to sit here waiting for the server queue. And I don't seem to be the only one who thinks so. Is it wrong that I kinda like launches like this https://t.co/Ibjayw6N25 — Geeky Pastimes (@geekypastimes) November 4, 2026 6:05 pm: I'm back in the queue, but this time with 2,135 people ahead of me. I just went to the forums to check if other people are having problems, and the forums are down. Let me know down below if you're able to get in. 6:00 pm: And here we go, World of Warcraft Forever is live, and I was immediately greeted by a login queue. But only with 128 people ahead of me. Not bad! Lets see if I get in. Well, I got in, but all the rulesets are 'temporarily unavailable.' Cool. 5:50 pm: Servers are up in 10 minutes, or at least they're supposed to be. But with the level of excitement that people have for WoWF, I wouldn't be surprised if the servers struggle for a little bit. But no matter what happens, remember, you will get in eventually. IF YOURE IN LINE AT THE WOW FOREVER LOG IN SCREEN STAY IN LINE DONT LEAVE THEY LEGALLY HAVE TO LET YOU IN THE SERVERS PER THE CONSTITUTION KNOW YOUR RIGHTS 🇺🇸 🇺🇸 — Krista (@KristaStreams) November 4, 2026 5:36 pm: The first legendary weapon in World of Warcraft Forever is a healing weapon called Taldramir, The Whispering Wood. It's cool enough that Blizzard is showing love to healers, but apparently it also had it made in real life, too . I'm getting ready for the launch by logging into retail just one more time before Forever kicks off in earnest. And, of course, the first thing I see is someone in trade chat saying "alright kids see you in a couple months or years depending on how good Forever is" A legendary stream deserves a new Legendary Weapon 💥 Introducing Taldramir, the Whispering Wood, forged in partnership with @WetaWorkshop 🔨 https://t.co/D3orhPhcM0 — World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) November 4, 2026 5:15 pm: We're 45 minutes out, but people already seem excited to get in. One Last Time. by u/Jescar1 in wowforever Today I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. Tomorrow I am playing World of Warcraft forever. The next day I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. The day after that I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. The day after that I am playing World of Warcraft Forever. Forever. — gloomi 🚬🌧 (@gloomi_x) November 4, 2026 Once again, my wife decided we needed a cake for launch day by u/kenshin138 in wow Congratulations to the entire @Warcraft team and best of luck on a great WoW Forever launch! Also wishing a speedy recovery to everyone who suddenly came down with the flu this morning 😔👀 — Marcus Kretz (@MarcusKretz) November 4, 2026 Everyone In The Queue Tonight by u/kainxavier in wowforever 5:00 pm: The servers are scheduled to go online in about an hour, and just in the last couple of days there's been a lot happening for WoW Forever. For instance, in response to the patch notes that went out Monday night, the Shaman class discord shut down in protest of the changes, something that happened with ret Paladins last year in Midnight. Still, the biggest question on my mind ahead of the launch is 'how will the servers handle the load?' Even in the best case scenario, I expect some pretty beefy server queues that we'll have to sit through. And, as a reminder, there are new Nvidia graphics drivers, so if you're on a Team Green card, take this hour before launch to update your drivers.

items.title: Scarlett Johansson Says The Batman: Part 2 Role Caused 'Existential Angst'
items.excerpt: While she didn’t disclose the character she’s playing, Scarlett Johansson says her role in The Batman: Part II has given her “a lot of existential angst” because it was “hard to crack."
items.content_text: While she didn’t disclose the character she’s playing, Scarlett Johansson says her role in The Batman: Part II has given her “a lot of existential angst” because it was “hard to crack.” The Black Widow star was interviewed by Entertainment Tonight about her new movie Paper Tiger, where she was asked which of her roles in upcoming franchise films (Exorcist: Martyrs or The Batman: Part II) pushed her the most outside of her comfort zone, “Probably the role in The Batman, because it gave me a lot of existential angst, for some reason,” Johansson explained. “It was very hard to figure out. I don’t know why, whether it was just the role or it was just where I am in my life, but it was just hard to crack it. And that’s all I can say about it.” The rumor mill has suggested Johansson is playing Gilda Dent or Poison Ivy in the sequel. Johansson isn’t the only cast member who’s been asked about The Batman: Part II in recent interviews. Robert Pattinson has praised the sequel for having " an understanding of Bruce Wayne and Batman's psychology " that he doesn't "think has been seen before." The Batman: Part II has resumed filming in the UK under the supervision of Steven Soderbergh , who is overseeing the final stages of shooting while director Matt Reeves deals with a family matter . Reeves will resume the directing reins once the film reaches post-production. Despite the production delays, The Batman: Part II remains scheduled to open in theaters on February 18, 2028.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever Review So Far - Beta Impressions
items.excerpt: 30 hours with Forever's beta provides an optimistic start to a long journey.
items.content_text: Editor's Note: This initial review-in-progress is based entirely on time spent in the pre-release beta, and will be updated as we get deeper into into the full game. I was there, Gandalf. I was there when the World of Warcraft opened its servers for the first time in 2004 – which might not literally be 10,000 years ago, but sometimes it feels like it. And now that I've put a good 30 hours into the beta for World of Warcraft: Forever, I'm looking forward to today's launch in a way I haven't for almost any game in a long time. GTA 6 can wait. It may surprise you to hear me say that and then follow it up with the fact that I had essentially zero interest in World of Warcraft: Classic back in 2019. In fact, I wrote one of my favorite articles ever about exactly why that was. But Forever is different. It's built on the bones of Classic, but with just the right amount of modern sensibilities baked in. There are new zones to discover, much-needed class changes, and some truly impressive graphical enhancements. So, I invite you to come on this journey with me, as it's going to be a bit different from our typical game reviews. Blizzard really wants Forever to be about the journey, not the destination – and we plan to honor that in this review. The thing is, Forever is made to be savored. I almost didn't want to review it at all, given how deadline pressure can sometimes warp the experience of something this big. Blizzard really wants this new take on their storied MMO to be about the journey, not the destination – and we plan to honor that here. This will be more of a long-form critique that's going to hearken back to an old Blizzard motto from their golden age: It will be done when it's done. Anything less wouldn't be a review of World of Warcraft: Forever so much as a review of rushing through World of Warcraft: Forever in a stressful and unintended way. As such, I plan to update this piece as I climb my way to level 60 and discover all the new things there are to discover at the sort of pace I think would make sense if I didn't have a hard deadline. I still expect to have some kind of a firmer verdict before everyone wanders off for the December holidays. But if you want to know whether I think it's worth jumping in right now, on launch day, I can start by sharing my impressions from the beta. They Cooked As an avid player of Modern WoW until very recently, and someone who skipped Classic altogether, it's almost a revelation to open up my character sheet in Forever and see 23 years of what I can only describe as "streamlinesh**tification" stripped away. Like, dang, this used to be so much more of an RPG! All the modern game's stat pruning, summary execution of mechanics that added character but were demonized as "inconvenient," class role homogenization, and so much more added up to a death by thousands of cuts that you almost wouldn't notice if you stayed subscribed from the beginning because it was generally so gradual.I love having features like parry, block, and hit chance back. I love leveling up my different weapon skills when I hit a new level. I love that we have more secondary stats to worry about than just crit, haste, versatility, and mastery. I even love having to go buy my skill ranks every level, because it makes me learn where the hub for my class is in each major city and meet the key NPCs I can hang with and look up to. I love that levelling actually takes a long time. This was important stuff that was slashed to try and create a frictionless slope that would never alienate anyone ever, and the modern game is much poorer for having lost it. Azeroth is so much more interesting to explore on foot, too. Flying mounts are fun, especially with the post-Dragonflight skyriding system. (They are!) But zooming around through the air as the default mode of travel has taken so much of the character of exploration and discovery out of Modern. Forever insisting that you spend the first 40 levels without even the speed boost of a ground mount allowed me to reconnect with this world in ways that really made me feel 14 again. It feels big and dangerous and mysterious. It's wonderful. From what I've seen so far, I think they might have done it – let's see if they can keep it up to level 60. And at this point, Forever's new lighting and post-processing make it look better than Modern to me. Yes, I do play with HD models. Sorry to all the SD purists, but I don't think the player races in particular actually hold up visually in 2026. I'm glad we can both pick the graphics we prefer. But regardless, these zones look stunning. They did go overboard with the fog in some areas, I think. But overall, I love the enhancements and going back to Modern feels like a straight downgrade. I do have some concerns already. One of them is the "realmless" structure, which I think is particularly bad for roleplayers like me. We fought against capital cities having phasing in Modern for a good reason. Splitting up these hubs where people go to find RP tends to do the opposite of building strong communities. Blizzard has been swearing up and down that this is good for the long-term health of Forever. I am completely unconvinced so far, but willing to at least give it a chance. It's hard to say too much more than that at this point. I ended my beta journey at level 13, gazing out across the dusty plains of Westfall, because I didn't want to spoil too much for myself before the big day. But from what I have seen so far? I think they might have done it. They made me believe I can go home again – and that home is somewhere I want to spend more time, with new surprises to discover. Let's see if they can keep it up for 47 more levels. Watch this space for updates in the weeks to come.
items.title_en: World of Warcraft: Forever Review So Far - Beta Impressions

items.title: Leonardo DiCaprio and Joaquin Phoenix Were Offered the Role of the Joker in The Dark Knight, But Turned it Down
items.excerpt: Leonardo DiCaprio and Joaquin Phoenix were both offered the role of Joker in The Dark Knight, but ended up turning it down, according to the film's casting director.
items.content_text: Leonardo DiCaprio and Joaquin Phoenix were both offered the role of Joker in The Dark Knight , but ended up turning it down, according to the film's casting director. When speaking at the Nashville Film Festival (via TV Intelligentsia and Batman News ), Christopher Nolan's longtime casting director John Papsidera revealed that Heath Ledger was not the first choice for Joker in The Dark Knight. He said the script was sent to Leonardo DiCaprio first, who apparently didn't even respond. Then, the offer went to Joaquin Phoenix, who would later win an Oscar for the same role in 2019's Joker . Phoenix told Nolan and Papsidera at the time that he wasn't interested in doing big movies and declined the part. Eventually, they landed on Heath Ledger, and the rest is history. Leonardo DiCaprio went on to star in Nolan's next project, Inception. The actor also stated last year that The Dark Knight was his favorite Nolan film. Warner Bros. reportedly pressured Nolan and his creative team to cast the Titanic star as The Riddler in the third Batman movie . The team went against this idea, since they typically developed the story for Batman first and then tried to figure out a villain. As a result, Bane made for a more logical villain in a story about an aging Batman who is physically outmatched. And as already noted, Phoenix went on to play a completely different version of the Joker. In his two films, Joker is far less calculated. He's more of a guy who stumbles into becoming a symbol for chaos, revolution, and anarchy, though is wildly out of his depth. While it may be difficult to imagine DiCaprio as Joker, it's worth reflecting on who Heath Ledger was before he was cast in the role. He was considered a pretty boy in Hollywood, not unlike DiCaprio, and it was seen as an odd choice to cast the actor for such a villainous role. Phoenix wasn't too far beyond that class of actor, either. It seems like Nolan and Papsidera were intentionally trying to play against type and find someone who could channel an unseen part of themselves.

items.title: GTA 6 Rakes in Over $750 Million in Preorders 2 Weeks Ahead of Release Date
items.excerpt: Data compiled by analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 has already raked in more than $750 million in preorders across both PlayStation 5 and Xbox.
items.content_text: Data compiled by analytics firm Sensor Tower estimates that GTA 6 has already raked in more than $750 million in preorders across both PlayStation 5 and Xbox. GTA 6 launches in just two short weeks. It’s one of the most highly anticipated video game releases of all time and possibly the biggest pop culture phenomenon of this decade. The hype for this particular entry is off the charts, and fans of Rockstar’s open-world action-adventure franchise are putting their money where their mouths are. According to data aggregated by Sensor Tower , Rockstar has already made three-quarters of the way to a billion dollars in preorders alone. As of November 3, an estimated 7.71 million units have been sold, translating to a whopping $751 million in profits. The split between consoles is also notable; the amount of preorders on PlayStation is significantly higher than those on Xbox, with a 74% - 26% split. This means that, on PlayStation, roughly $559 million in revenue was accrued; on Xbox, $192 million was made. Rockstar is making out like bandits, and the game hasn’t even come out yet. For reference, GTA 5 made $800 million in its first 24 hours , and reached $1 billion in three days , making it the fastest entertainment product to reach $1 billion in history. It's possible that GTA 6 blows past this record, given what we're already seeing, but only time will tell once November 19 actually gets here. These numbers are huge, and it’s likely due to fans purchasing the $100 Ultimate Edition of the game rather than its standard version. Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar's parent company Take-Two Interactive, said as much in an August interview with CNBC , where he theorized this trend was “a reflection of the fact that the most avid consumers are the ones who are preordering now." The Standard Edition of GTA 6 isn’t a whole lot cheaper. At $80, the base game also costs players a pretty penny — something that Zelnick told IGN was a reflection of the game’s value and actually a “bargain.” “We aim always to deliver vastly more value than what we charge,” he said. “And we think that price point allows us to do just that. And then of course we have a premium opportunity for people who want to avail themselves of that. And even that one, again, we think is priced in a way so as to deliver much more value than what we're charging,” he told us. “The truth is that the real cost of a AAA video game is a whole lot lower today than it was 20 years ago. Pricing has not kept pace with inflation. And our goal is to continue to over-deliver for our consumers, because how you feel about any experience is the intersection of the experience itself and what you pay for it. So to say that we expect that Grand Theft Auto 6 will be an incredible bargain as experiences go is a gross understatement, because Rockstar Games is known for over-delivering.” GTA 6 releases on November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox X|S. For more interesting stats about the game, check out IGN’s report on how many players intend to take off work on release day, or see the concerning amount of fans who would give up their pets for a month for the chance to play it a week early.

items.title: Adam Driver Says He's Done Playing Kylo Ren, but Would Return if Someone Revived His Canceled Solo Film
items.excerpt: Adam Driver says he's done with Star Wars and Kylo Ren, but would be open to a return if someone revived his cancelled solo film.
items.content_text: Adam Driver says he's done with Star Wars and Kylo Ren, but would be open to a return if someone revived his canceled solo film. Last year, Adam Driver and director Steven Soderbergh dropped a bombshell on Star Wars fans: They were working on a new film centered around Kylo Ren . It was meant to be a sequel to The Rise of Skywalker, which would have resurrected the somewhat redeemed sequel trilogy antagonist. However, Disney said no... because they couldn't buy into Kylo Ren coming back from the dead. The film was tentatively titled The Hunt for Ben Solo, and Star Wars leadership like Kathleen Kennedy also backed the project , but the bosses at Disney weren't as convinced. Driver and Soderbergh developed the film for two years and seemed to be pretty passionate about it. However, Driver has given up hope of it ever happening, even in spite of fan campaigns . When speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Driver was asked if he had a future in Star Wars. He stated that it was "over" and there would be "no more Star Wars" for him. Eisen asked if he would come back if The Hunt for Ben Solo were revived by Disney, and Driver said that he would, but he believes "the ship has sailed." This aligns with Lucasfilm boss Dave Filoni saying the movie was not in active development earlier this summer. As a result, you probably shouldn't hold out hope for this film ever getting made. Despite the fact that fans are consistently in a state of fury about the status of the Star Wars franchise and this movie was something they all rallied behind, Disney isn't interested. It's also possible that Disney is trying to move on from the sequel trilogy, which got a progressively sour reputation with each installment. Disney is currently working on Star Wars Episode 10, with Spider-Man: No Way Home director Jon Watts in the driver's seat. It's unclear if the likes of Rey or Finn will reprise their roles in the project, or if Disney is going to create more distance between those films. Steven Soderbergh has moved on from Star Wars and is now helping direct the final weeks of production on The Batman Part 2. The Oscar-winning filmmaker stepped in to help Matt Reeves, who had to depart the production during filming due to a personal matter. Soderbergh is working under the direction and vision of Reeves, with the intent to pass the baton back to him for post-production. Soderbergh himself has expressed disinterest in returning to The Hunt for Ben Solo , believing if it was going to happen, it would've already happened.

items.title: Mob Entertainment Lays Off 'Almost Entire' Escape From Playtime Team
items.excerpt: A former member of Mob Entertainment’s Escape from Playtime Team claims “almost all” staff working on the project have been laid off.
items.content_text: A former member of Mob Entertainment’s Escape from Playtime Team claims “almost all” staff working on the project have been laid off. The news comes from a LinkedIn post penned by a former lead game designer at the studio on November 4, 2026. “Today is a tough day,” they wrote. “Mob has laid off almost the entire Escape From Playtime team, including myself. If anyone knows of any work that I or any of the team affected can do, please reach out. This industry is tough, but the people band together to help each other out. Today that help is needed. “For my friends affected at Mob I'm sorry, we did an amazing job, and pushed out a fantastic game. Be proud of what we accomplished. For those at Mob not affected, I will miss you all. Thank you for the opportunity to make EFP. Back to the grind.” Escape From Playtime is an online survival co-op game for two to eight players based on the horror mascot Poppy Playtime franchise. In the game, teams play as Smiling Critters plushes as they scavenge for resources and avoid monstrous mascot monsters. The spinoff was released on October 21, 2026; with so many staff being laid off just two weeks later, fans understandably grew worried about the game’s future. Luckily, it has been confirmed that Escape From Playtime is still sticking around — at least, for now. On the game’s official Discord channel, Mob Entertainment's senior communications manager Tyler Sanchez spoke out about the layoffs and vaguely hinted at what’s next for the game. Sanchez said that development on the title will continue, outlining several improvements that are planned based on players’ feedback thus far. “We've had to make the incredibly tough decision to part ways with some talented members of our team who helped bring Escape From Playtime to life. These are people who poured their creativity and passion into building this game and making it something special. We're incredibly grateful for everything they've contributed, and we want to take a moment to recognize the people behind the work. This isn't the kind of news we ever want to share, and we know it's difficult to hear, especially for a community that cares so deeply about the game and the people who make it,” he wrote. “We also know that this will carry uncertainty from many of you about the future of Escape From Playtime. To be clear, development on the game continues. We've already made changes to the roadmap based on your feedback, including improvements to matchmaking, the order in which we'll roll out bigger body enemies, making the existing map more diverse and interesting, and much more. “We know that news like this can bring a lot of questions, and it's important to us that we're transparent about where things stand. While we don't have every answer to share just yet, we'll continue to communicate the development process with you all.”
items.title_en: Mob Entertainment Lays Off 'Almost Entire' Escape From Playtime Team

items.title: Maya Hawke Gets ‘Key’ Role in Live-Action Magic: The Gathering Movie
items.excerpt: Maya Hawke has been cast in a ‘key’ role for Legendary’s live-action Magic: The Gathering movie, which is also planned to have a television series.
items.content_text: Maya Hawke has been cast in a "key" role for Legendary’s live-action Magic: The Gathering movie, which is also planned to have a television series. Magic: The Gathering’s live-action adaptation seems to have finally found its footing, with Deadline reporting that Stranger Things star Maya Hawke is the first actor to be officially cast in the film. Sources told the outlet that Hawke’s role is a "key" one, and that the project will have an "ensemble" feel. The same insiders said producers were focused on making sure she got the first offer to join. It seems that Legendary and Hasbro have big plans in mind, as the iconic trading card game franchise is also set to receive a television universe. Canadian actor/director Matt Johnson is set to direct and write the film, alongside co-writers Aidan Fitzgerald and Noah Gardner. Matt Johnson is best known for BlackBerry, a comedy-drama about the BlackBerry phone, and Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie, a sci-fi-ish comedy movie based on a web series he co-created. His filmography is a bit sparse, but given his comedy chops — along with Deadline’s report of an "ensemble cast" — it seems like the Magic: The Gathering movie could have a similar tone and feel to Dungeons and Dragons: Honor Among Thieves . This is the latest news from this movie to surface after it was first confirmed in 2025 when Hasbro and Legendary announced their partnership and intentions to make an MTG movie. In July 2026, Vulture confirmed Matt Johnson’s involvement in the project, with storyboard artists, costume designers, and location scouts from Dune also reportedly lending their talents to the film. Magic: The Gathering has faced decades of difficulty in its attempts to snag a screen adaptation. Its struggle first began in 2008, when Hasbro struck a deal with Universal to make movies based on several of its big brands, including MTG. Unfortunately, this project died a slow and painful death and, by 2012, it was ultimately canceled. 20th Century Fox (now 20th Century Studios) then snagged the film rights to Hasbro’s card game in 2014, which again sat in limbo until card designer Mark Rosewater confirmed the project was dead in 2022. This was especially painful, as several big names were attached to Fox’s MTG movie; Simon Kinberg ( X-Men: Days of Future Past ) was set to supervise, and Bryan Cogma — a writer for Game of Thrones — was also brought in to write the film. Netflix also tried to snag a piece of the pie in the early 2020s with a live-action movie and an animated series that, unsurprisingly, also went nowhere. Now, Legendary and Hasbro are working hand-in-hand to finally bring MTG’s vibrant universe from cards to screens. This is the latest big adaptation news to come from Legendary after the release of its Street Fighter movie this October, which proved to be a mixed bag among fans and critics but managed to secure top spot in the box office during its opening weekend. K-pop girl group IVE is bringing its hit 2022 song "Love Dive" to the battle royale shooter, complete with themed locations, character skins, choreography, and music videos — further proof there is no scenario that cannot be improved with a bit of K-pop. The collaboration is live now on PC and arrives on console November 12, bringing three special IVE locations across Rondo, all inspired by the "Love Dive" music video, including the IVE Mansion. We're also getting all six members represented with character likenesses, outfits, accessories, and weapon and gear skins. That mode runs from November 18 to December 2 on PC and November 26 to December 10 on console. items.title: Texas' New Attorney General Composed the Soundtrack for 67 Episodes of Dragon Ball Z's English Dub
items.excerpt: Nathan Johnson was just elected as the new attorney general of Texas — but before he was in politics, he actually composed the music for 67 episodes of Dragon Ball Z.
items.content_text: Nathan Johnson was just elected as the new attorney general of Texas — but before he was in politics, he actually composed the music for 67 episodes of Dragon Ball Z. The United States midterm elections took place yesterday, November 3. The country’s Democratic party saw several major victories in this election, with the state of Texas being one of the most notable; for the first time in 30 years, the state ‘turned blue,’ with Democratic candidates James Talarico elected as U.S. senator and Gina Hinojosa as governor. Another Democratic candidate who won the vote was Nathan Johnson, who was elected as Texas’ attorney general. Besides being the state’s first Democratic AG since 1994, he’s making headlines for a different, rather unexpected reason: He once composed the soundtrack for English episodes of Dragon Ball Z . Johnson opened up about his past with the franchise in a June 22 Facebook post , where he described what it was like working on the famous anime series while being a father to young children. “If you grew up watching Dragon Ball Z, you might know me better than you think: I composed the musical scores for 67 episodes and five movies, and had a great time doing it. Catching up recently with Taylor Rehmet, we talked about how composing for DBZ influenced my direction, and how the show still connects with so many Texans today,” he captioned the post. “I had a one-year-old at the time, and I remember him sitting on my knee and stuff blowing up [on screen], and he’s like, ‘Oh, daddy, Goku!’ He just thought it was super cool. Even then, it got me street cred with my kids’ friends, and it gave me a creative outlet and a cultural connection that very few people have had the opportunity to have,” he said in his conversation with Rehmet. Nathan Johnson was fascinated with music as a child, but decided to pursue a law degree in university, which has since come in handy in this recent election. However, before he became attorney general, he put his legal career on hold to pursue music, eventually crossing paths with one of Funimation’s co-founders, Robert Cocanaugher. Cocanaugher was the landlord of a house he was hoping to rent. In a beautiful coincidence, this led to him being hired on as the second composer for Funimation’s in-house English dub of Dragon Ball Z. He was the last replacement composer used for the company’s dub, or any other English version of the anime, due to the Funimation’s music branch getting axed to cut costs. Johnson spoke about his time at Funimation in an August 2012 interview with The Dao of Dragon Ball, saying he was nearly ready to quit his struggling music career when he first met Cocanaugher. “A place near my house was for rent. I called the number on the sign out front to rent an office, and the guy on the phone said, ‘What will you use it for?’ I said ‘To practice law, but to be honest, I might throw an electric keyboard in there and make some musical noise, but nothing to disturb the other tenants.’ He said, ‘What kind of music?’ Well, it turned out the person on the phone and the owner of the building was Robert Cocanaugher," he said. “I had never seen Dragon Ball, never heard of Dragon Ball Z in my life. Never seen an episode of an anime in my life. I had never scored anything commercial in my life. But Barry and obert apparently liked my music,” he continued. “...It was one of the most bizarre collisions of circumstance I’ve ever experienced.” Johnson isn’t the only political candidate going viral for their connections to the entertainment space. Republican Marty O'Donnell, who composed music for the original Halo games and Destiny at Bungie, was the subject of a joke by winning Democratic opponent Susie Lee, who poked fun at his loss by posting the famous Vine of college students singing Halo’s monk chant in a bathroom.

items.title: The Avengers #1 Review: A Marvel Relaunch Done Right
items.excerpt: The Avengers #1 is a strong start for the relaunched series, and a promising sign that Marvel is finally righting the ship when it comes to one of its most important franchises.
items.content_text: Marvel's flagship Avengers series hasn't been in the greatest shape for the past decade. Even with very talented creators like Jason Aaron and Jed MacKay steering the ship, the franchise has struggled and largely failed to recapture the appeal of the Brian Michael Bendis and Jonathan Hickman eras. With this latest relaunch, Marvel has pinned all of its hopes on writer Chip Zdarsky and artist Marco Checchetto, the team responsible for one of the best Daredevil runs of the 21st Century. It turns out that they may be just the team to put this book back on track at long last. Given the Daredevil pedigree, there was no way I wasn't going to be checking out this new series. That said, I did have certain reservations coming in. The team roster is oddly similar to that of Bendis' New Avengers run (albeit with the recently revealed Miracleman joining the fray). Is this merely a quick-and-dirty attempt at hearkening back to a better era for the series? Fortunately, there's a logic to which characters are included here, and the execution is different enough that this doesn't simply read like a retread of New Avengers, even if it definitely shares elements in common. The basic idea here is that Zdarsky and Checchetto's Avengers chronicles the formation of a very different team in the wake of Avengers: Armageddon. The old guard have all tapped out for one reason or another, leaving the likes of Spider-Man, Wolverine, the aforementioned Miracleman, and a battered and brooding Captain Marvel to fill the void when the world cries out to be saved again. Like the 2004 New Avengers, this is a team brought together by circumstance rather than one that's been actively recruited. That generally seems to be the way to go for this franchise. While there's only so much team-building that can be done in a first issue, Zdarsky wastes no time in taking advantage of these intriguing character dynamics. Obviously, we know he can write a mean Matt Murdock. But this isn't simply a retread of his past run. Zdarsky instead focuses on immediately forging a bond between Matt and Carol Danvers, the latter of whom is still adjusting to a new world where her powers are a shadow of their former self. I don't know if Daredevil/Captain Marvel shippers were a thing before now, but they certainly will be. The creators also wisely hinge a lot of this first issue on Spider-Man. Spidey is very much the moral center of the book, the one most agitated by the absence of the Avengers and the generally frosty response the public has toward superheroes at the moment. Obviously, this isn't Spidey's first go-round as an Avenger, but this feels like a turning point for the character. His mantra about power and responsibility becomes all the more critical in a time when there's no one else to be an Avenger. Zdarsky understands these characters and what motivates them, and he makes the most of that in bringing the new team together. Zdarsky understands these characters and what motivates them, and he makes the most of that in bringing the new team together. And, yes, the book looks fantastic. Though that's hardly a surprise. Checchetto is coming off an incredible run working with Hickman on Ultimate Spider-Man, and he brings all the same strengths to bear on this new assignment. His figure work is stunning, as always, marked by elegant line-work, sunbtloy expressive faces and that trademark lovely hair only Checchetto can pull off. The general storytelling is equally impressive. Zdarksy's script gives Checchetto a nice balance of intimate character moments and large-scale action, and he handles both very adeptly. Matt Wilson's colors seal the deal, creating a tone that's both inviting and just a bit eerie where needed. It's also worth pointing out how well this first issue integrates itself into current Marvel continuity. Not only does the series build very neatly out of Zdarsky's recent work on Armageddon and Captain America, but it reflects the current statuses quo of the various Avengers as the characters come together (including Spidey's current Aunt May predicament ). Not in a way that punishes readers for not following the various other titles, but simply in a way that makes the current Marvel Universe feel a little more cohesive and united.
